convoLines.text: "Can I tell you something? I have been lying about my age — I'm younger than I look."

"Thank you. ...I needed someone to know, and I needed it to stop there."

"We went over this," Sofia says, a little tired. "I already told you the truth about that."
"Any regrets? The real kind, not the small stuff."
They take it in and give nothing back. Not yet.
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Still on that question."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"This was good." They mean it.
"Can I tell you something? I've been writing letters I'll never send. I'm ashamed and I can't stop."

"Do you believe in anything? Now, I mean. After everything."

"What's something you're good at that nobody here knows about?"
"Noted. Filing that under 'extremely useful.' The village needs that. ...if that makes sense."
"Still on that question. I mean it."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"That can wait — it isn't going anywhere. What's on your mind?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "The whole fire was arguing about Buffering last night — what to even CALL it. 'Big Ugly' got shouted down. What's your vote?"
"Go on, then. I'll be thinking good thoughts at you."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"About the pantry run — I hate to ask twice, but it's still open. Will you?"
"The stores won't stretch past tomorrow, and I'm not choosing who eats. Nobody's worked the old burn east of camp in days. We'll fill packs before dark."

d86: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Bridget Domingo is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d86: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d86: 🕯️ Bridget is dead — and the dead hold no treaties. Every link Haven has shakes.
d86: 🕯️ Bridget Domingo is dead — the wild. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d86: What Bridget kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d86: No one is left to pick up the Codex. The village dies out — quietly, the way villages do. The season ends here.
